data.title: About Coursecraft
data.intro: A small catalog of practical courses taught by independent instructors.

children.text: Coursecraft is sample content for a course website theme. It shows how an independent instructor or a small training business can present courses so that learners can answer three questions quickly: Is this course for me? What will I learn? Who will guide me?
How courses work here

Every course page lists its level, learning outcomes, prerequisites and a curriculum overview. Some courses link to the instructor's own course platform; others invite you to send an enrollment inquiry, and the instructor replies directly.
What this site does not do
This website describes courses. It does not host lessons, take payments or create learner accounts. Those happen with the instructor or on the linked course platform.
All people, courses and organisations shown in this sample are fictional.

data.title: Contact
data.intro: Questions about a course, a start date or a group booking? Send us a note.

children.text: Use the form to ask about any course, or email us directly. Mention the course name if your question is about a specific course.

data.name: Maya Ellison

photo.alt: Portrait of Maya Ellison smiling, wearing white headphones

data.short_bio: Maya has spent twelve years designing everyday software and now teaches the practical side of UX: research you can run this week, sketches that settle arguments, and prototypes people can actually test.

children.text: Maya Ellison is a fictional instructor created for the Coursecraft sample content. In this story she started as a print designer, moved into product design, and led small design teams before turning to teaching full time.
Her courses favour short exercises over long lectures. Each lesson ends with something you make: a sketch, a research note, a flow, or a clickable prototype you can share for feedback.

data.name: Theo Brandt

photo.alt: Theo Brandt in glasses, seen from the side while working at a desk

data.short_bio: Theo builds websites for small organisations and mentors career-changers learning to code. He teaches the web platform first and tools second.

children.text: Theo Brandt is a fictional instructor created for the Coursecraft sample content. In this story he has worked as a freelance web developer for nonprofits, local shops and studios.
He believes most people learn to code fastest by shipping small, real pages, so every module in his courses ends with a working page you keep.

data.name: Priya Natarajan
data.short_bio: Priya teaches photography and study skills to busy adults. Her lessons are short, practical and built around what you already carry: a phone or a simple camera.

children.text: Priya Natarajan is a fictional instructor created for the Coursecraft sample content. No profile photo has been added yet, so the theme shows her initials instead.
She combines a background in documentary photography with years of coaching adult learners who fit study around work and family.

data.title: UX Design Fundamentals
data.summary: Learn how to research, sketch and test simple product ideas so the things you design are easier to use.
data.format: Self-paced online lessons with weekly exercises

cover_image.alt: Notebook with hand-drawn interface wireframes beside a laptop and a coffee mug

children.text: This course introduces the everyday habits of user experience design. You will practise talking to people about how they work, turning what you hear into simple flows, and sketching screens quickly before anything is built.
It suits people starting out in design, as well as developers, marketers and founders who want to make better decisions about the products they work on.

outcomes.outcome: Plan and run a short interview with a potential user
Turn research notes into a clear problem statement
Sketch and compare several layout ideas quickly
Build a simple clickable prototype and test it with two people

prerequisites.item: A laptop and a free account with any prototyping tool

curriculum.lessons:
What UX design is (and is not)
Planning a five-question interview
Listening for problems, not features

From notes to patterns
Writing a problem statement
Simple user flows

Fast sketching techniques
Comparing layout options
Choosing what to prototype

Building a clickable prototype
Running a short usability test
Deciding what to change next

faq.question: Do I need to buy software?
faq.answer: No. Every exercise can be done with free tools or pen and paper. The lessons show one free prototyping tool, but you can use any you like.

faq.question: How much time should I plan for?
faq.answer: Most learners spend about three hours a week: one hour of lessons and two hours on the exercise.

faq.question: How do I join?
faq.answer: Send an enrollment inquiry from this page. The instructor replies with the next start date and how to get started.

Images and alternative text

The box model revisited
Flexbox in practice
Grid for page layouts
Responsive type and spacing
Designing for small screens first

The DOM in plain language
Events and simple interactions

When not to use JavaScript

Checking accessibility basics
Performance quick wins
Publishing your pages
Planning what to learn next
Final project review

faq.question: Where are the lessons hosted?
faq.answer: On the instructor's own course platform. This site only describes the course; enrollment and lessons happen at the course link.

faq.question: Is this suitable for complete beginners?
faq.answer: It assumes you have written a little HTML. If you have not, start with a beginner course first.

data.title: Photography for Everyday Life
data.summary: Take calmer, clearer photos of the people and places around you with the camera you already own.
data.format: Short lessons with weekly photo walks

cover_image.alt: A camera on a wooden table in front of hills at sunset

children.text: A gentle introduction to photography built around short weekly photo walks. You will learn to notice light, frame a scene with intention and choose your best shots.
Any phone or simple camera works. The focus is on seeing, not on equipment.

outcomes.outcome: Use natural light to improve everyday photos
Compose scenes with simple framing rules
Edit a photo lightly without overdoing it
Curate a small, consistent set of your images

prerequisites.item: Time for one short photo walk each week

curriculum.lessons:
Morning, midday and evening light
Shade, windows and reflections
Photographing people kindly

Framing and simple lines
Getting closer
Backgrounds that help

Picking your best frames
Light-touch editing
Building a small photo set
Sharing your work

faq.question: Do I need a professional camera?
faq.answer: No. Every exercise is designed for a phone or a simple camera.

faq.question: Are there live sessions?
faq.answer: No live sessions are included. Lessons are short and self-paced; the instructor answers questions sent through the inquiry form.

data.title: Clear Writing at Work
data.summary: Write emails, briefs and updates that colleagues read once and understand.

cover_image.alt: A hand writing notes with a pen in an open notebook

children.text: A focused course on plain, structured workplace writing. Each lesson takes one common document and shows how to make it shorter and clearer.

outcomes.outcome: Lead with the point in emails and updates
Structure a one-page brief
Cut jargon without losing precision

prerequisites.item: Regular writing as part of your job
A few recent emails or documents to practise on

curriculum.lessons:
Writing the first sentence first
Subject lines that work
Updates in three parts

The one-page brief
Headings that guide readers
Plain words, precise meaning
Editing your own draft
Asking for useful feedback

faq.question: Can I bring my own documents?
faq.answer: Yes. The exercises work best with real (non-confidential) writing from your job.

data.title: Advanced Interface Prototyping

cover_image.alt: The back of a laptop on a desk next to a mug that reads A Brighter You

children.text: For working designers who already prototype and want to model realistic states, data and transitions. You will prototype one complex flow end to end and test it.

Prototype with realistic content and data
Design transitions that explain change
Plan and run a moderated test of a complex flow

A portfolio project you can extend

curriculum.lessons:
